title: Annotatio VI §.I: Same kind as intramural Lutheran or Reformed disputes — does not derogate Ecclesiastical Union
pass_a_gloss: This Class of Theological controversies, to whatever number it is finally extended, between Lutherans and Reformed, as to the matter, is no other than such as still flourishes among Lutherans themselves (e.g. on Omnipresence and Multipresence of Christ’s Body) or among the Reformed (e.g. on Universal and Particular Grace) — derogating nothing whatever from Ecclesiastical Union.
pass_b_english: As to the matter, this class between Lutherans and Reformed is no different from disputes that still run inside each camp — Lutheran fights over the body’s omnipresence and multipresence, or Reformed fights over universal and particular grace.
While it lasts, it takes nothing away from church union.
source_text: Haec controversiarum Theologicarum Classis, ad quemcunque tandem numerum extensâ, Lutheranos inter & Reformatos, quà rem, non alia est, quàm qualis inter ipsos vel Lutheranos, e. g. de Omnipraesentia & Multipraesentia Corporis Christi; Vel Reformatos, e. g. de Universali & Particulari Gratia, adhuc dum viget, Unioni Ecclesiasticae nihil quicquam derogans.
